proof_summary: Pair the valid summands by the involution \((n,k,j)\mapsto(j+k,k,n-k)\), which preserves \(N=n(k+1)+(n+1)j\) and the binomial weight, so nonfixed pairs cancel modulo 2. At a fixed point, either \(k=n\) and \(j=0\), giving \(N=n(n+1)\), or the weight contains the even central binomial coefficient \(\binom{2(n-k)}{n-k}\); hence an odd total forces the former case.
